source.title: On Empirical Comparisons of Optimizers for Deep Learning
source.authors: Da-Mi Choi; Christopher J. Shallue; Zachary Nado; Jaehoon Lee; Chris J. Maddison; G. Dahl

record.tranche_reason: The study compares optimizer generalization across tuning protocols and workloads, using its own experiments and reproductions of prior protocols.
record.gate_note: Tests V4 through optimizer comparisons under limited and expanded tuning. The paper’s reported performance values are mainly presented in figures; precise values cannot be reliably assigned from the supplied flattened text. Cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Own experiments compare held-out performance under restricted and expanded optimizer tuning, directly testing V4. Restricted protocols reproduce adaptive-optimizer disadvantages; expanded searches eliminate or reverse them. The study is an original source for V4, so no verdict labels are assigned.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Within the tested workloads and tuning protocols, more general optimizers did not underperform their included special cases after extensive tuning, and restricted-search rankings could collapse or reverse when tuning expanded. The authors caution that detailed findings depend on workload and protocol and that batch-size effects were not tested.
record.recipe_differences: Optimizer comparison study with extensive optimizer-specific hyperparameter tuning; it also reproduces selected restricted-tuning protocols from Wilson et al. (2017) and Schneider et al. (2019).
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer ranking changes with the tuning protocol and search space. Workload also changes whether optimizer performance separates clearly.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimizer inclusion relationships also predict steps to a validation target; on Transformer, Adam requires 60% as many steps as Momentum to reach the target.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With sufficient hyperparameter tuning, optimizer inclusion relationships can predict training speed as well as final predictive performance.

fits_no_version.finding: The Transformer implementation jointly removes dropout and separates input and output embedding matrices because the authors observed better performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Joint implementation changes can improve this Transformer language model; this does not isolate dropout's effect in classifiers.

record.problems: The authors caution that findings depend on the tested workloads and tuning protocol; the study did not vary batch size. Results are mostly plotted, and some comparisons have no textual numeric values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows kept for Figure 1 optimizer-by-optimizer comparisons: the text reports the aggregate inclusion relationship for each workload, while the plotted values are figure-only and cannot be reliably assigned to individual optimizers from the flattened text.

untested.parts: No comparison of fitting random labels and generalizing on natural labels.
No width sweep across or beyond interpolation.

No controlled test of switching Adam to SGD or of decoupled weight decay as the cause of recovery. The restricted-tuning comparisons do not establish that worse held-out performance occurs despite equal or better training performance. Results do not establish universality across workloads or tuning protocols.
Batch size is fixed within each workload; no large-versus-small-batch comparison.
No controlled dropout comparison in classifiers, training-set-size sweep, or test of excessive dropout.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with generalization gaps.
No identification and removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

missing.what: The CIFAR-100 comparison includes two intermediate protocols absent from the rows: tuning the learning-rate schedule alone, and tuning optimizer parameters with a constant learning rate. These distinguish schedule effects from optimizer-parameter effects. Their optimizer-specific rankings cannot be reliably read from the supplied flattened figure.
missing.locator: Figure 4, CNN on CIFAR-100 middle two groups; Appendices D.7.2 and D.7.3

record.verdict_notes: This study is explicitly an original source for V4; labels are therefore empty. States for expanded-tuning rows refer to V4 as written, including its explicit allowance for elimination or reversal of the adaptive disadvantage. Figure-only numeric values have not been reconstructed. The reported 77.1% ImageNet validation accuracy is the authors' own result, but its 76.5% comparator is a cited result from Goyal et al., not a controlled within-study comparison.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test all image-classification and language benchmarks named in the version, or whether broader tuning universally removes or reverses optimizer differences.

rows.subject: VGG on CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Compared optimizer test error after matching Wilson et al. (2017)'s grid search over initial learning rate only.

conditions.value: initial learning rate only; Wilson et al. protocol

rows.value: RMSProp and Adam had worse test error than SGD and Momentum under the reproduced protocol.
rows.note: The paper says this reproduces the original result; exact values are figure-only.
rows.check: The condition names only RMSProp, but the value combines RMSProp and Adam. Split these comparisons or name both optimizers. This is a reproduction using validation-based trial selection, rather than an exact replication of Wilson et al.'s selection procedure.

source_check.correct: The result covers both RMSProp and Adam versus SGD and Momentum. Initial learning rate is grid-searched with a fixed decay schedule. Choi selects trials by validation performance, differing from Wilson's training-based selection.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.3, Figure 3 leftmost group, footnote 3; Appendices C and D.5.1.
source_check.problem: The condition names only RMSProp, but the value combines RMSProp and Adam; matching Wilson's protocol also needs the trial-selection qualification.

tranche.reason: Own optimizer comparisons vary tuning protocols to test the same held-out-performance question, including V4's broader-tuning qualification.

source_check.notes: Expanded-tuning rows observe V4's explicit qualification. Appendix C reports unequal trial budgets for some protocol comparisons; Figure 9 does not establish paired training performance before and after expansion. The authors' conclusion is accurately scoped; no verdicts apply to this original source.
